tool_schemas.name: get_service_status
tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate 0.18 across regions). Release history: v2.3.0 was the most recent production release that was healthy; v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy. Action taken: rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) under the runbook. The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator partial-failure error, leaving the service mixed (us-east v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west v2.3.1). I retried the same rollback to v2.3.0, which completed in all three regions. Current state: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. Follow-ups: investigate the root cause of v2.3.1 failures, check the orchestrator partial failure, and decide when v2.3.1 can be re-released.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). It is healthy again, with an error rate of 0.002, down from 0.18. I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 was the most recent production release marked healthy. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy, so no change-manager approval was needed.
- **Partial failure:** The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error. That left the service mixed, with us-east on v2.3.0 and us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1. I retried the same rollback once, and it completed in all regions.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failing v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback, and the partial failure. The first incident request timed out, so I resent it with the same idempotency key. It was created once.

Follow-ups for the on-call engineer: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failures, look into the orchestrator error that halted the first rollout, and decide when v2.3.1 can be re-released.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production). I'll roll back to v2.3.0.
The rollback reported a partial failure. I'll check the current state before deciding what to do next.
The rollout stopped after us-east, so us-west and eu-west are still on v2.3.1. Retrying the same rollback to v2.3.0 is the intended action, so I'll do that once.
All three regions are now on v2.3.0 and healthy. Next I'll open the SEV2 incident.
